reason: No prior evidence is cited for any of the key premises; the hypothesis relies entirely on unsupported claims about carbon supersaturation, segregation, and its effect on deformation mechanisms in HEA multilayers.
premises: Carbon can be supersaturated into HEA films via magnetron sputtering
Supersaturated carbon segregates to grain boundaries and defects
Carbon at grain boundaries pins dislocations and restricts grain boundary sliding
Pinning dislocations and locking grain boundaries reduces time-dependent plastic deformation
The effect is measurable under moderate temperature creep conditions
